Kolobrzeg Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kołobrzeg, Poland

Demolished. This is Kołobrzeg's Old Jewish cemetery, granted by the city magistrate in 1815, after which the Jews of Kołobrzeg no longer had to bury their dead in neighboring Gryfice or Świdwin. By 1885, the site had run out of burial space and was closed by police order, with the community shifting to a new cemetery on Kösliner Straße, documented elsewhere in this collection; around 1937, authorities forced the community to clear the old site, though only the larger, more valuable monuments were relocated to the new cemetery's entrance. Complete devastation followed during Kristallnacht in November 1938. In 1995, illegal treasure hunters searching for precious metals inadvertently rediscovered the site, unearthing Hebrew-inscribed tombstones; a lapidarium incorporating matzevot from both of Kołobrzeg's cemeteries was formally opened there in 2000.
